changes: Weekday normalized: 'roja 6' = Friday (śukravāra), not left as raw string
Purpose reworded: 'śrīrāmārpaṇam astu' is a dedication formula (merit offered to Rāma), not svārtha/parārtha
Notes expanded: date check, nature of the second colophon, Tīrthanātha absent

notes: The catalogue gives Tīrthanātha as the scribe, but that name does not appear in the quoted colophon. He may be named elsewhere in the manuscript; he is not added here. The last passage is the sub-colophon of the commentary Adhyātmarāmāyaṇasetu by Rāmavarman, son of Himmativarman. His virudāvalī ('sakalarājavipaduddharaṇasamartha...') marks him as a ruler, but he is the commentator, not the reigning king of this copy. The date VS 1958 Bhādra śukla 1, roja 6 (Friday) works out to about 13 September 1901 CE. That fits the weekday and agrees with the catalogue's VS 1958. 'sālamiti' and 'roja' are Persian-derived Nepali/Hindi dating terms.
